comparisons.peer_summary: Corporate Audit and the Chief Audit Executive (CAE) maintain independence from Financial & Legal Units (FLUs), Group Risk Management (GRM), and other control functions by reporting directly to the Audit Committee, while the CAE also administratively reports to the CEO.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America establish Internal Audit as an independent function with a dual reporting line: functional reporting to the Audit Committee for independence and administrative reporting to the CEO for operational purposes. Citi explicitly states it is independent of the first and second lines, while BAC similarly defines its independence from FLUs and GRM. Additionally, both disclosures highlight the objective assurance role of Internal Audit towards the Board and regulators.

sentences.text: Internal Audit is independent of the first line, second line and enterprise support functions.
The Citi Chief Auditor manages Internal Audit and reports functionally to the Chair of the Citi Audit Committee and administratively to Citi's CEO.
Corporate Audit and the CAE maintain their independence from the FLUs, GRM and other control functions by reporting directly to the Audit Committee.
The CAE administratively reports to the CEO.

comparisons.peer_summary: Internal Audit serves as the third line of defense, reporting to the Audit Committee and CEO, and is responsible for independently assessing and validating the effectiveness of key controls within the risk management framework.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and Citi both define Internal Audit as the 'third line of defense' that reports functionally to the Audit Committee and administratively to the CEO. Both disclosures emphasize the function's responsibility to provide independent assessment and validation of key controls and risk management effectiveness to the Audit Committee, senior management, and regulators.

sentences.text: The Citi Chief Auditor manages Internal Audit and reports functionally to the Chair of the Citi Audit Committee and administratively to Citi's CEO.

The role of Internal Audit is to provide independent, objective, reliable, valued and timely assurance to the Board, its Audit Committee, Citi senior management and regulators over the effectiveness of governance, risk management and controls that mitigate current and evolving risks and enhance the control culture within Citi.
Internal Audit is considered our third line of defense, and our director of Internal Audit reports to the Audit Committee of the Board and administratively to our chief executive officer.

Internal Audit is responsible for independently assessing and validating the effectiveness of key controls, including those within the risk management framework, and providing timely reporting to the Audit Committee of the Board, senior management and regulators.

comparisons.peer_topic: Three lines of defense model and responsibilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm employs a "three lines of defense" model for risk management. The first line (LOBs, Treasury, CIO) owns risks and executes controls; the second line (IRM) independently measures and challenges risk activities and sets policies; the third line (Internal Audit) provides independent assessment of governance and controls.
comparisons.comparison: JPMorgan Chase and Citi both describe Internal Audit as the third line of defense, led by a chief officer (General Auditor at JPM, Chief Auditor at Citi) who reports functionally to the Audit Committee and administratively to the CEO. Both companies frame Internal Audit's core role as providing independent/objective assessment of governance, controls, and risk management effectiveness.

sentences.text: The Citi Chief Auditor manages Internal Audit and reports functionally to the Chair of the Citi Audit Committee and administratively to Citi's CEO.
Internal Audit is independent of the first line, second line and enterprise support functions.
The Internal Audit function is led by the General Auditor, who reports to the Audit Committee and administratively to the CEO.

The third line of defense is Internal Audit, an independent function that provides objective assessment of the adequacy and effectiveness of Firmwide processes, controls, governance and risk management.

comparisons.peer_topic: Internal Audit Reporting Lines and Additional Activities
comparisons.peer_summary: The Chief Audit Officer reports directly to the Board Audit Committee (BAC) Chair and administratively to the CEO, reporting results quarterly to the BAC and periodically to other committees, while IAD may also conduct requested retrospective reviews or investigations.
comparisons.comparison: Morgan Stanley mirrors Citi’s governance structure for Internal Audit, where the Chief Audit Officer reports directly to the Audit Committee (BAC) Chair and administratively to the CEO. Both disclosures utilize the same reporting architecture to ensure the independence and objectivity of the internal audit function.

sentences.text: The Citi Chief Auditor manages Internal Audit and reports functionally to the Chair of the Citi Audit Committee and administratively to Citi's CEO.

The Chief Audit Officer, who reports directly to the Chair of the BAC and administratively to the Firm's Chief Executive Officer ("CEO"), communicates the results of IAD activities to the BAC on a quarterly basis and periodically to the BRC and BOTC.
